headline: Somatic variant calling shifts onto pangenome and germline-composite references, with long reads for SVs
label: Pangenome Based Somatic Variant Calling
summary: Three preprints and a published benchmark apply pangenome or composite germline references to somatic SV and variant detection, with long-read tumor-normal data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is somatic variant discovery anchored to germline-informed references rather than GRCh38. A published benchmark reports that graph and personalized pangenomes improve somatic variant calling accuracy relative to GRCh38. Two preprints extend this to structural variants from long reads: JANUS works directly on tumor-normal pangenome graphs from HiFi reads without prior alignment, and VESPA-SS finds tumor-specific strings against a draft composite germline reference. The new element is making the germline-aware reference or graph the primary frame for somatic analysis. Cycle-Extractor, which reconstructs ecDNA cycles from short- or long-read breakpoint graphs, addresses complex somatic events but does not itself use a pangenome reference. Other items on aDNA alignment and ONT direct-cDNA preprocessing are only loosely related.
